newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-YANKS' TORRE, RANGERS' OATES JOINT A.L. MANAGER OF YEAR.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-YANKS' TORRE, RANGERS' OATES JOINT A.L. MANAGER OF YEAR.

text.p: On the day his brother walked out of a hospital with a new heart, the New York Yankees' Joe Torre shared the American League Manager of the Year award with the Texas Rangers' Johnny Oates.

Torre, who guided the Yankees to the Eastern Division title, the American League pennant and the World Series championship, and Oates, who led the Rangers to the A.L. West title, each received 89 points, the Baseball Writers of America announced on Thursday.
Oates got 12 first-place votes, two more than Torre. Torre had 12 second-place votes to eight for Oates, who got five third-place points, two more than Torre.

It was just the fifth tie for an award from the Baseball Writers of America, who also select Most Valuable Players, Rookies of the Year and Cy Young winners. It was the first time the managerial award was shared.

A magic number for both managers was 36. Oates got the Rangers into the postseason for the first time in the team's 36-year history, while Torre made the World Series for the first time in his 36-year playing and managerial career.

Torre's first season in New York ended in a thrilling World Series title for the Yankees, the first for the team since 1978. But postseason achievements were not considered because the voting was conducted before the playoffs.
New York fans embraced Torre, a 56-year-old Brooklyn native, not just because of the Yankees' exploits on the field, but also because of his personal story this year.
His brother Rocco died during the regular season and his brother Frank received a heart transplant during the World Series and went home, the operation apparently a complete success, two weeks later.
Torre, the 1971 National League Most Valuable Player, helped New York win the Eastern Division title with a 92-70 record, the Yankees' first outright division title in 17 years.
Torre is the third former MVP to win Manager of the Year, joining Frank Robinson and Don Baylor.

The 50-year-old Oates led the Rangers to a 90-72 record and their first American League West title in his second season as the team's manager. Texas was eliminated in the division series by the Yankees, three games to one.

Lou Piniella, the 1995 A.L. Manager of the Year, finished third behind Torre and Oates with 35 points, including three first-place votes. Mike Hargrove of the Cleveland Indians was fourth with 22 points and two first-place votes, while Detroit Tigers manager Buddy Bell surprisingly got the other first-place vote and finished fifth.

Buck Showalter, whom Torre replaced, was the A.L. Manager of the Year two years ago, giving the Yankees two of the awards in three years. Yankee shortstop Derek Jeter was announced earlier this week as the A.L. Rookie of the Year by unanimous vote and New York pitcher Andy Pettitte is the league's likely Cy Young winner.
The National League Manager of the Year award will be announced Friday.
